- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to historical mean or recent peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is trending upward, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently overestimates in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; apply slight downward bias (−0.5% to −2%) for short-term.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model tends to lag mean reversion; align forecast with 3–5 day moving average of true prices for smoother transitions.
- For 10+ day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply correction based on 15-day rolling average of true prices, especially if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment is consistently low and price is trending down, model often undercorrects; add 1–3% downward bias to avoid false optimism.
